project.name: Acme User-Branch Service (UniBasic -> Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 feasibility POC)
project.description:
Feasibility POC for a prospective client engagement: equipment-finance ILS system, business logic in Rocket UniData/UniBasic, target Java 17+. Translates two REAL, public UniBasic routines (github.com/zelenko/pick — no repo-level LICENSE stated, used here read-and-analyze/attributed, not redistributed) from a signed unibasic spec (spec/v1, schemaId=unibasic, targetStack=java-spring):
- add-branch-to-user.pick: the CONVERT VM TO @FM / LOCATE / INSERT / CONVERT @FM TO VM round-trip becomes a plain List<String> add-if-absent (the mark-conversion dance is unnecessary once the data lives in a real collection) plus a READV/WRITEV-by-bare-number field access made explicit as a named property with a citation back to the unresolved DICT position. - ARRAY.PICK: the same LOCATE-then-insert-if-missing idiom in isolation, demonstrating the resolved List shape independent of the file-access wrapper.
Builds OFFLINE through the maven-sidecar (pinned plugins + junit/assertj only). UniData/UniVerse have no free/scriptable runtime (Rocket's only free tier was a superseded 2-user dev/demo edition; Rocket's own MV BASIC tooling is a VS Code extension that talks to a live licensed server, not a standalone interpreter) — so source-execution equivalence is NOT claimed here. The golden score + this compiling, passing JUnit suite are the gates, same honest posture as the OpenEdge ABL archetype.
